​@mcdonaldswasfaraway VIT Bhopal issue refers to a major health crisis and subsequent student uprising in late 2025. there were no reported on-campus deaths linked to the jaundice outbreak.(Acco to the uni at that time, later found to be 3) However, rumors of casualties, combined with poor living conditions and administrative heavy-handedness, ignited mass, violent protests.

Here are the details of the incident:

The Health CrisisThe Outbreak: In November 2025, dozens of students at the VIT Bhopal campus in Sehore, Madhya Pradesh, fell ill with jaundice and typhoid symptoms, which were linked to contaminated drinking water and poor food quality in the hostels.

Contamination: Government inspections of campus water samples later confirmed that several samples were contaminated with E. coli bacteria.

The Death Rumors: The protests were partially sparked by panic over rumors that three students had died from the outbreak.

Official Clarification on Deaths: The administration and local authorities clarified that there were no deaths on campus due to jaundice. A female student passed away at her home in Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), but official medical reports indicated it was due to Tuberculosis (TB), unrelated to the campus outbreak.

The Protests and EscalationStudent Outrage: Frustration had been brewing for weeks over unaddressed complaints regarding foul-smelling water and unhygienic mess conditions.Violence: On the night of November 25, the situation escalated dramatically. Following allegations that wardens and security staff assaulted students who were complaining, approximately 4,000 students went on a rampage.

Property Damage: The protesting students vandalized university property, including the chancellor's residence, laboratories, and hostels, and set fire to multiple vehicles, including buses and an ambulance.

Official Inquiry and ConsequencesGovernment Probe: Following the violence, a three-member committee was formed by the Madhya Pradesh Private University Regulatory Commission (MPPURC).

Scathing Findings: The probe’s report criticized the university’s administration, accusing them of trying to cover up the jaundice outbreak, failing to address basic health and hygiene issues, and operating under a "fear-based" disciplinary system that suppressed student voices.

Action Taken: The state government issued a show-cause notice to the VIT administration regarding the lapses and insensitivity toward student welfare. Police also registered FIRs against wardens and staff members for assaulting students

I believe the professors at Patna University are truly excellent and dedicated. Every professor I’ve had the chance to learn from has taught really well and given their best in class.

But most of the problems here are related to infrastructure, which professors cannot do anything about. In fact, even their own safety isn’t guaranteed—sometimes bombs are thrown at their cars by students from the boys’ hostel.

As for student leaders, honestly, they are of no real help either. More than half of them are just involved in hooliganism and misbehavior rather than actually solving student issues.

I still remember one day when our Vice Chancellor came to the Department of Political Science at Darbhanga House. He asked students if they faced any problems in class. Some of my classmates mentioned genuine issues like frequent power cuts and broken boards. But instead of addressing those concerns, the Vice Chancellor started sharing stories from his childhood—how he used to cross a river just to attend school. Rather than acknowledging our current problems, he was more focused on narrating his own struggles from the past.

बिड़ला समूह ने गांधी के समय “हरिजन सेवा” का नारा देकर खुद को समाज सुधारक दिखाने की कोशिश की, लेकिन सच्चाई यह है कि उनकी संस्थाएँ शोषित समाज को कभी असली प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं दे पाईं। उदाहरण साफ़ है—BITS Pilani। वर्ष 2025 में यहाँ कुल 5,137 छात्र हैं, जिनमें SC सिर्फ़ 29 (0.5%) और ST मात्र 4 (0.08%) हैं, जबकि राष्ट्रीय औसत (AISHE 2022–23) के अनुसार उच्च शिक्षा में SC ~14.7% और ST ~5.6% है। यानी जहाँ 15% SC और 7.5% ST होना चाहिए था, वहाँ बमुश्किल आधा प्रतिशत भी जगह नहीं दी गई। यह दिखाता है कि गांधी–बिड़ला की “हरिजन सेवा” की बातें केवल प्रतीकात्मक थीं।


दूसरी ओर, यही बिड़ला समूह उद्योग में सरकार की नीतियों का सबसे बड़ा लाभार्थी है। Hindalco Aluminium और UltraTech Cement दोनों ही भारत की टैरिफ और एंटी-डम्पिंग नीतियों के सहारे प्रतिस्पर्धा से बचते हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, 2023 में भारत ने विदेशी एल्युमिनियम फ्लैट प्रोडक्ट्स पर 10% से 15% इम्पोर्ट ड्यूटी लगाई और चीन व UAE से आने वाले कुछ उत्पादों पर एंटी-डम्पिंग ड्यूटी ₹4,000–₹6,000/टन तक लगाई, जिससे Hindalco सुरक्षित रहा। इसी तरह सीमेंट क्षेत्र में UltraTech को 2024 तक उच्च आयात शुल्क और घरेलू प्राइस कंट्रोल का सीधा लाभ मिला।


यहाँ गहरी विडंबना है—एक तरफ़ BITS Pilani में शोषित समाज (SC/ST) को 98% सीटों से बाहर रखा गया, दूसरी तरफ़ बिड़ला उद्योग अपने मुनाफ़े के लिए सरकार की नीतियों पर पूरी तरह आश्रित है। यानी समाज सुधार का दिखावा कर जनता को मूर्ख बनाना, और सरकार से सुरक्षा लेकर प्रतिस्पर्धा से बचना—ये दोनों बातें मिलकर साबित करती हैं कि भारत का कॉरपोरेट ढांचा नैतिक रूप से खोखला है। यह विरोधाभास बताता है कि गांधी–बिड़ला की “हरिजन सेवा” एक ढोंग थी, क्योंकि जिनको uplift करना था वे आज भी बाहर हैं, जबकि जिनके पास पूँजी है वे अब भी सत्ता की टैरिफ ढाल के पीछे छिपकर फायदा उठा रहे हैं।

Institutes like IITM and VIT produce strong medical research, yet much of it stays as data on paper without moving into real hardware implementation. Funding for prototyping can still be managed through alumni and external donations, but bringing these ideas into actual use requires clinical trials and collaboration with major hospitals like AIIMS.

comment_text:
The Hidden Cost of Rankings: How NIRF and Star Ratings Are Hurting Education

In recent years, the higher education landscape in India has become increasingly driven by ranking systems like NIRF (National Institutional Ranking Framework) and initiatives such as the Institution Innovation Council (IIC) star ratings. While these mechanisms were originally introduced to encourage quality, innovation, and accountability, they have inadvertently created a troubling reality on the ground — one that is damaging the very essence of teaching and learning.

Today, teachers — who should be spending their time mentoring students, teaching deeply, and pursuing meaningful research — are often reduced to clerks compiling endless data for rankings. Instead of designing better lessons, developing new skills, or conducting impactful research, faculty members are pressured to fill forms, chase documents, and provide evidence for every activity.

The situation is even worse in private institutions, where the pressure to showcase high rankings and five-star ratings is relentless. These institutions often see rankings as marketing tools rather than as measures of quality. 

The result?

Syllabus portions are rushed through to meet timelines.

Students are neglected, receiving less personal attention and mentorship.

Teachers are overloaded, unable to focus on academic depth or professional growth.

The ultimate losers in this system are the students. They lose access to passionate, well-prepared educators who might have otherwise inspired them, guided them in research, or helped them think critically. Instead, they are left with hurried lectures and surface-level learning.

It’s time for parents, policymakers, and educational leaders to recognize this imbalance. If an institution spends more energy chasing rankings than nurturing its students, its priorities are misplaced. Data collection should be handled by dedicated administrative teams, allowing teachers to do what they are meant to do — teach, mentor, innovate, and inspire.

True quality education cannot be measured by rankings alone. It is reflected in the growth, curiosity, and success of students — and that should always remain the ultimate goal.

video_title: A little view of my college | BML Munjal University #tanvisharmayt
comment_text:
@Raj_ftw first we fill the from from ther website, then they will ask either for jee result or cuet, then some days later you are gonna have a interview, then after some days you will give the bmusat exam. All these notifications will be received on your respected mail account only, so make sure to give the one which is available all the time, if possible give yours.
At my time, I filled up the form before jee mains session 2, so after the results were declared I submitted the scorecard of result and after they confirm like if we are eligible (>55/60%ile) then we will have a interview which will be taken by an individual person. In interview, they will be asking these questions (these were the question I was asked)
Q1. Give your introduction.
Answer should be like this,
My name is .......... and I am from ....... district, ........... (state name). I have passed 12th boards with ......% and in jee mains/ cuet my score was ......... .
Q2. What was the reason that your score was less?
Ans. Sir/ma'am, actually it was because that I wasn't able to get proper guidance and much support because of my coaching/ institute, I lacked in the performance, but I am sure that in the upcoming exams I will do my best
Q3. What are your hobbies?
In here tell your hobbies and in my case, I had a hobby of drawing so I told about that and there they asked me to show if I had any, but unfortunately they were missing, and I told other hobby like to reverse engineer my toys and see how the mechanism works inside it (it's just too common in boys like to open the toys, take out the motor etc. whi khilone todna krna. Now this might seem pretty awkward to listen but since you already mentioned that specific word "reverse engineering" and that actually comes under kinda skill as you get to know about many new components and the mechanism. So for a normal person, this might sound shit to them but for the prof. and to other educated people, this is what not so many people do and is actually good, so don't feel like this won't sound good, it will actually help you).
Apart from this I told that in my 8th class there was a science exhibition, and in there me and my friend made a project together which was based on converting mechanical power to electrical power, like by rotating the dc motor in anti direction to supply the current to a connected LED.
And I again asked if I had that project, but mere neech dost the to unhone pata nhi kha guma dia vo to koi dikkat nhi thi mene bol Diya tha ki, that project is at my friend's house.
And agar aapke bhi kuch hobbies ho to vo add krdena remember one thing, sometimes things might sound stupid, but if it works it's not stupid.
Q4. (If they ask you about your qualities say this)
My qualities are, time management, interest in learning new skills(but in this case they might ask you what skills you learnt, so make sure to say this only if you learnt some extra skills or else don't take risk) , positive attitude, managing high stress, good temper.

(Now from here your 11th and 12th knowledge will be challenged(

Q5. If three forces are applied on an object, at what angle they should be applied and how much to keep the net force 0 or to keep the object in equilibrium?
(The answer I gave was)
Let say the value for three forces was 5N, so they will be placed at 120° from eachother to keep the object in equilibrium.

Q6 (This question was kinda challenging as you will know the trick used to check mind)
If have this glass (he showed me the glass) full of water, then how will I measure the no. of molecules present?
Ans. So first, we will put the glass filled with the water on a weighing machine and note the weight, then will empty the glass and note the weight again. Then we will reduce the weight of glass from the weight of glass filled with water so as not get calculation errors. Now the weight we obtain is the weight of the water, so to get the no. of moles, we know that 1 mole of water is equal to 18 grams, so we will divide the obtained weight by 18 and we will get the no. of moles. Now to calculate the no. of molecules, we will multiply this with Avagadro's constant Na that is 6.022 × 10^23 and the number obtained is the no. of moles.

The reason for this question to be a bit challenging was because we had to reduce the weight of glass from the weight of glass filled with water.

⚠️these were the questions I was asked, you might be asked some different questions too but make sure to remember those first 4 questions as it tell so much about you⚠️
Then the prof. and me had some normal convo. and at the end, before leaving say them this "Thanks for having me". Not many know this phrase but this is a very respectful phrase.
⚠️KEEP THE WHOLE CONVERSATION IN ENGLISH⚠️

now after some days of interview you will be notified about the sat exam and with that exam they will get to know about your brain thinking levels. The exam have maths, aptitude, English ntse level 2
According to my percentile I scored in this exam, I was 4th ranked from all the students and recently when I checked again just in timepass I was 7th.
The percentile you obtain, suppose you obtain 90%ile and 250 students gave the exam so your rank will be like this,
(90/100)×250 =225
This means 225 students as behind you, so your rank will be 250-225= 5th

So this was all, I hope I cleared all of your doubts and how the process will be, still if you have any you can ask me here anytime.

comment_text:
"One of my friends took admission in Computer Science at SRM Institute of Science and Technology. Even after receiving a scholarship, the total cost of his four-year degree was around ₹26 lakh. After graduation, he secured a placement with a package of only ₹8 lakh per annum.
On the other hand, I studied at L.D. College of Engineering, a government engineering college in Gujarat, where the total tuition fee for four years was approximately ₹30,000. I was placed with a package of ₹12 lakh per annum.
This shows that many students and parents are influenced by flashy marketing, grand campuses, and brand names. Some families are even willing to take on heavy financial burdens or sell valuable assets to secure admission to expensive private universities. However, the true value of education is measured by knowledge, skills, and career opportunities—not by how much a university charges in fees.
Students and parents should carefully evaluate factors such as academic quality, faculty, industry exposure, research opportunities, and actual placement outcomes before making a decision. A high fee does not automatically guarantee a better future.
Many government engineering colleges across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and other states provide excellent education and strong placement opportunities at a fraction of the cost. Education should be about empowering students and building careers, not merely about generating revenue through aggressive marketing and high fees."

"मेरे प्रिय भारतवासियों—

मेरा एक दोस्त—होनहार, मेहनती, टॉप का छात्र—SRM यूनिवर्सिटी में गया।
कंप्यूटर साइंस, 4 साल, स्कॉलरशिप के बाद भी फीस—26 लाख रुपए।
और 4 साल की जलन, झूठे सपने और रात-दिन की मेहनत के बाद प्लेसमेंट में उसे मिला?
एक मज़ाक—₹8 लाख का ऑफर।

अब सुन मेरी कहानी—मैं गया गुजरात की सरकारी इंजीनियरिंग कॉलेज—LD अहमदाबाद।
4 साल की फीस? ₹30,000—एक मिड-रेंज मोबाइल से भी सस्ती।
और मेरा प्लेसमेंट? ₹12 लाख—साफ़, सच्चा, बिना किसी झंझट के।

अब इस पागलपन को देखो—
26 लाख = 8 लाख।
30 हज़ार = 12 लाख।

ये शिक्षा नहीं, ये सरकारी लूट है।

SRM, VIT—ये यूनिवर्सिटी नहीं, भ्रम के कारखाने हैं, जो मिडल-क्लास परिवारों के खून-पसीने और आँसुओं पर चलते हैं।
इनका बिज़नेस मॉडल सीधा-साफ़ है—सपने बेचो बड़े-बड़े, और पहुँचाओ नरक में।

माँ-बाप अपना घर बेचते हैं, सोना बेचते हैं, अपनी बुढ़ापे की जमा-पूँजी बेचते हैं—सोचते हैं 'बड़ा नाम' खरीद रहे हैं।
लेकिन असल में खरीदते क्या हैं?
उम्र भर की EMI, बच्चे का कुचला हुआ आत्मविश्वास, और एक ऐसी डिग्री जो जिस कागज़ पर छपी है, उससे भी कम क़ीमती है।

और इनका सबसे बड़ा हथियार? डर।
हर माँ-बाप के कान में फूँकते हैं—"सरकारी कॉलेज बेकार हैं। निजी नाम ही असली हैं।"
सालो, ये झूठ है।

मैंने देखा है। मैंने जिया है।
गुजरात, महाराष्ट्र, राजस्थान, तमिलनाडु—हर राज्य की सरकारी इंजीनियरिंग कॉलेजें योद्धा बनाती हैं, भिखारी नहीं।
वहाँ दमदार फैकल्टी, असली मुकाबला, और ऐसे प्लेसमेंट जो इन तथाकथित 'प्रीमियम' यूनिवर्सिटियों को शर्म से झुका दें—और वो भी उस फीस में, जो ये निजी माफ़िया सिर्फ एक दिन के ओरिएंटेशन में वसूल लेते हैं।

तो सुन मेरी बात—तीखी, साफ़, और धमाकेदार:

तुम शिक्षा नहीं खरीद रहे, तुम एक ब्रांड का टैटू खरीद रहे हो जो जीवन भर तुम्हें रोएगा।

SRM और VIT—एक ही गंदगी के दो मुँह हैं।
ये बेशर्म, बेरहम, खून-चूसने वाले पिशाच हैं, जिन्होंने अकादमिक गाउन पहन रखा है।
इन्हें तुम्हारे बच्चे से कोई मतलब नहीं—इन्हें तो तुम्हारे बैंक बैलेंस से प्यार है।

हर माँ-बाप को जो ये पढ़े—
अंधे मत बनो। किसी दिखावटी नाम के चक्कर में अपना भविष्य न गिरवी रखो।
तुम्हारे बच्चे को असली कला चाहिए, नकली चमक नहीं।

हर छात्र को जो ये पढ़े—
भेड़ मत बनो। इन शिक्षा-दलालों के जाल में मत फँसो।
चुनो बुद्धि को, चुनो सरकारी को, चुनो ईमानदारी को—लालच को नहीं।

क्योंकि जिस दिन तुम्हारा बेटा 26 लाख की डिग्री लेकर 8 लाख की नौकरी में घुटेगा,
और मेरे सरकारी कॉलेज वाले दोस्त का 12 लाख का पैकेज चमकेगा—
उस दिन तुम्हें पता चलेगा—तुम माँ-बाप नहीं, ग्राहक बने थे।
और SRM, VIT—वो ठग थे।

सावधान हो जाओ।
वरना बर्बाद हो जाओगे।
ये फैसला तुम्हारा है—और ये जानलेवा गंभीर है।"😢
